blocks.raw: ## Configuring Organisation Unit (OU) support for product entities
blocks.text: Configuring Organisation Unit (OU) support for product entities

blocks.raw: <Glossary>Organisation Unit</Glossary> (OU) support for product entities enables you to use the same SKU codes for the different OUs under an organisation.
blocks.text: Organisation Unit (OU) support for product entities enables you to use the same SKU codes for the different OUs under an organisation.

blocks.raw: > 📘 By default, transactions are tagged under OU. This is achieved by linking the stores where transactions occur to corresponding zones or concepts, and categorizing these zones or concepts as OUs.
blocks.text: By default, transactions are tagged under OU. This is achieved by linking the stores where transactions occur to corresponding zones or concepts, and categorizing these zones or concepts as OUs.

blocks.raw: ### Use case
blocks.text: Use case

blocks.raw: In your organizational setup, there are multiple organizational units (OUs) in place. By default, any inventory that's uploaded to the main organization is automatically shared among all these individual OUs.
blocks.text: In your organizational setup, there are multiple organizational units (OUs) in place. By default, any inventory that's uploaded to the main organization is automatically shared among all these individual OUs.

blocks.raw: However, let's consider a situation where a particular org unit requires its own separate inventory. This necessity arises due to conflicts noticed between the SKU codes it utilizes and those uploaded by other org units.
blocks.text: However, let's consider a situation where a particular org unit requires its own separate inventory. This necessity arises due to conflicts noticed between the SKU codes it utilizes and those uploaded by other org units.

blocks.raw: In such scenarios, you have the option to enable the "OU support for product entities" configuration. This configuration allows the creation of distinct inventories that are specific to each specific organizational unit.
blocks.text: In such scenarios, you have the option to enable the "OU support for product entities" configuration. This configuration allows the creation of distinct inventories that are specific to each specific organizational unit.

blocks.raw: ### Enabling OU support for product entities
blocks.text: Enabling OU support for product entities

blocks.raw: To enable OU support for product entities, create a [JIRA ticket](https://capillarytech.atlassian.net/browse/CAP-88674`) and enable the config `CONF_OU_LEVEL_PRODUCTS_ENABLED`.\`
blocks.text: To enable OU support for product entities, create a JIRA ticket and enable the config CONF_OU_LEVEL_PRODUCTS_ENABLED.`

blocks.raw: **Brand addition limits and error handling**
blocks.text: Brand addition limits and error handling

blocks.raw: When you add brands using the Intouch API or UI, the system enforces a maximum active brand limit for your organization. By default, this limit is 250 brands (controlled by the org\_product\_brands\_limit setting). If you try to add a brand and your organization already has the maximum number of active brands, the system blocks the addition and displays a validation error. You must deactivate or remove existing brands before you can add new ones if you reach this limit.
blocks.text: When you add brands using the Intouch API or UI, the system enforces a maximum active brand limit for your organization. By default, this limit is 250 brands (controlled by the org_product_brands_limit setting). If you try to add a brand and your organization already has the maximum number of active brands, the system blocks the addition and displays a validation error. You must deactivate or remove existing brands before you can add new ones if you reach this limit.

blocks.raw: **Important:** Adding brands using the Import Profile Add Brands does not enforce the org\_product\_brands\_limit. You can import brands in bulk using this profile even if your organization exceeds the default brand limit. However, brands added this way will still be subject to other validation checks.

blocks.raw: When you add a brand using the Intouch API or UI, you cannot exceed the maximum number of active brands allowed for your organization. The default limit is 250 brands. If you try to add a brand after reaching this limit, the system will show a validation error and block the addition. To add more brands, deactivate or remove existing brands first.
blocks.text: When you add a brand using the Intouch API or UI, you cannot exceed the maximum number of active brands allowed for your organization. The default limit is 250 brands. If you try to add a brand after reaching this limit, the system will show a validation error and block the addition. To add more brands, deactivate or remove existing brands first.

blocks.raw: Adding brands using the Import Profile Add Brands bypasses the brand limit. You can import brands in bulk even if your organization exceeds the default limit, but all other validations still apply.
blocks.text: Adding brands using the Import Profile Add Brands bypasses the brand limit. You can import brands in bulk even if your organization exceeds the default limit, but all other validations still apply.

blocks.raw: To add product brands, perform the following:
blocks.text: To add product brands, perform the following:

blocks.raw:
1. Click **Add New**.
2. In the **Name** text field, enter a name for the brand.
3. (Optional) In the **Label** text field, enter a label name.
4. (Optional) In the **Description** text field, enter a valid description for the brand.
5. If OU support is enabled, from the **OU code** drop-down, select the OU to which this size needs to be mapped. For more information, see [OU support for product inventory](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/inventory-profiles#configuring-organisation-unit-ou-support-for-product-entities).
6. (Optional) If applicable, from the **Parent** drop-down, select the parent brand.
7. Click **Save**

blocks.raw: ## Inventory import and category Creation Behavior
blocks.text: Inventory import and category Creation Behavior

blocks.raw: When importing inventory data, new product categories will NOT be created and existing category mappings will NOT be updated in incentives unless both of the following conditions are met:
blocks.text: When importing inventory data, new product categories will NOT be created and existing category mappings will NOT be updated in incentives unless both of the following conditions are met:

blocks.raw:
* The `CREATE_NON_EXISTING_CATEGORY` flag is enabled.
* The `INVENTORY_FIELDS_TO_UPDATE` configuration includes category fields.
blocks.text: The CREATE_NON_EXISTING_CATEGORY flag is enabled.The INVENTORY_FIELDS_TO_UPDATE configuration includes category fields.

blocks.raw: If these configurations are not set, imported SKUs may not appear in incentives due to missing category associations. To ensure that new categories are created and properly mapped during inventory import, verify that both the flag and the relevant fields are configured before starting the import process.

blocks.raw: **Note:** If you notice that imported SKUs are missing from incentives, contact the Product Support team and review your configuration for these settings.
